decisions.reason: Increasing paragraph spacing on content-heavy pages does not resolve or alter the title page's image and text composition.
The paragraph-spacing decision does not change chapter illustration placement, sizing, coverage, or rendering requirements; the image defects are separate observations.
The source does not change the copyright page publisher line or specify that the general spacing adjustment applies to that front-matter page.
Italicizing Mama's Hot Take text is an independent same-message requirement already represented in this candidate; the paragraph-spacing modification does not alter it.
Although spacing may affect pagination operationally, the source does not change the requirement to update table-of-contents page numbers after finalizing the book size.
Spacing between paragraphs does not change the Chapter 12 subtitle hierarchy, body-text role, or capitalization requirements.
The interior paragraph-spacing change is unrelated to the prohibition on a literal newline artifact in the book title.
The source changes general interior text spacing but does not alter the obligation to prepare back matter and author copy.
The authoritative manuscript version and content-preservation rule arise from a separate clause in the same message and remain unchanged by the layout-spacing decision.
The requested spacing applies to content-heavy interior pages and does not change the paperback cover artifact, content, dimensions, or review requirement.
Interior paragraph spacing has no necessary effect on KDP keyword content, its document delivery format, or its copy-and-paste use.
The client requests a formatting adjustment rather than a change to manuscript wording, approved passages, or the copyediting goal.
